cycle_position.summary: Grab-bag of operating-business-flavored niches. Car wash NNN: average listed cap 6.21% (April 2026), stable; Mister Car Wash-leased assets 5.25-6.25% on 20-year terms — express-tunnel saturation risk in overbuilt corridors is the known hazard. RV parks: observed caps span 5.13-8.86% by quality/seasonality. Parking and marinas: no clean 2026 national data in snippet coverage; both are municipal-contract/operations businesses at heart. Ground leases/towers: bond-like, institutionally priced.

supply_demand.value: Car wash: express-tunnel overbuilding in some corridors (tenant-failure risk behind the credit). RV: demand cyclical with fuel/consumer.

debt_terms.value: NNN forms finance like retail NNN; RV/marina/parking are SBA-or-operations territory.

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: Only the NNN forms behave like real estate (a car wash runs about $2M+ a ticket, the top of the range); the rest are operating businesses in a real-estate form.
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: A car-wash NNN repeats the retail NNN's role with worse residual risk (a single-purpose building if the tenant fails in an overbuilt corridor). RV parks and marinas can yield well but require hospitality operations.

gaps: Car-wash corridor saturation screen for any specific deal
